transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

A lazy yellow flame that produces black soot means the burner is not getting enough air, so the gas is burning incompletely. A healthy gas-hob flame should be mostly crisp blue.

Common causes include:

• Blocked burner holes or dirty burner cap — food spillages, grease, cleaning residue or moisture can disrupt the gas/air mix.
• Burner cap not seated correctly after cleaning.
• Blocked or incorrect injector (jet) — especially if the hob was converted between natural gas and LPG, or if a jet is partially blocked.
• Problem with the air supply, gas pressure, or burner assembly — this needs professional attention.

What to do:

1. Turn that burner off and let it cool.
2. Remove the pan supports, burner cap and burner ring, and clean the flame holes gently with a soft brush/wooden toothpick. Do not enlarge holes or poke metal wire into the injector.
3. Dry all parts completely and refit them squarely and securely.
4. Try it again.

If it remains yellow or sooty, stop using that burner and arrange for a Gas Safe registered engineer to inspect it. Incomplete combustion can produce carbon monoxide, so don’t try to adjust gas valves, jets or air settings yourself.

If you can smell gas, feel unwell (headache, dizziness, nausea), or the flame is large/uncontrolled, turn the appliance off, ventilate the room, avoid switches/flames, and contact your gas emergency service.
Thank you. I should mention that I've noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. Should I still try cleaning the burner first?

No — don’t use or test-clean the burner while you are also smelling gas with all controls off. The yellow, sooty flame needs attention, but an unexplained gas smell could indicate a leak from the hob, its pipework, or a control valve.

Do this now:

• Do not light the hob or any other flame, smoke, or use matches/lighters.
• Don’t operate electrical switches, plugs, extractor fans, or appliances near the smell.
• Open doors and windows to ventilate if you can do so without operating electrical equipment.
• If you know where the gas isolation valve is and can reach it safely, turn the gas supply off.
• Leave the property if the smell is noticeable or increasing, and call the gas emergency service from outside / a neighbour’s home.

If you’re in Great Britain, call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. In Northern Ireland, call 0800 002 001. If you use bottled LPG, contact the cylinder supplier’s emergency number instead.

Do not use that hob again until it has been checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Tell them both symptoms: gas smell when switched off, and a yellow sooty burner flame.
